newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac, Juppe up in opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac, Juppe up in opinion poll.

text.p: An opinion poll on Saturday confirmed that French President Jacques Chirac and his embattled Prime Minister Alain Juppe had regained some ground with voters following Chirac's long-awaited television interview a week ago.
An Ifop survey to be published on Sunday in the weekly Journal du Dimanche said 30 percent of voters were satisfied with Chirac, up from a near-record low of 27 percent last month.
Juppe benefited even more clearly from the December 12 interview, in which fellow Gaullist Chirac backed him despite sniping from the ranks of the ruling centre-right coalition.
The survey of 1,848 voters carried out in the days following the interview saw Juppe surging four points to 24 percent.
The poll confirmed an upward trend seen in other surveys this week, but the two leaders' gains came mostly from voters who had no previous opinion.
The percentage of dissatisfied voters remained far higher at 59 percent for Chirac and 67 percent for Juppe, down one point for each.
